subject: Deployment boundary acceptance checklist and owners
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@medicore.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up & acceptance checklist: Dedicated vs Private VPC

Hi Sophie — great discussion earlier today. Thanks for walking us through the primary constraints for Medicore's imaging pipeline. Per our call, the key qualification item is the deployment boundary: whether you will accept Redwood Dedicated (network-isolated tenant on shared infra) or require a Private VPC / customer-controlled on-prem deployment. To move forward, I drafted a concise acceptance checklist (attached) so each side has clarity on criteria, evidence, and owners.

Top-level asks we agreed on:
- Data residency and custody: Does Medicore require customer-controlled network egress and KMS? If yes, Private VPC or on-prem likely required.
- Audit trail & proof: For Dedicated we can provide per-tenant audit logs + SOC2 artifacts; for Private VPC you get full control plane logs and optional HSM integration.
- Key management: Can Medicore use Redwood KMS with CMKs, or must keys be in your HSM/KMS?
- Data persistence / backups: How long must user content be retained and who controls snapshots?
- Network controls: IP allowlist vs full VPC peering & private endpoints.

Requested next steps (internal + external owners):
1) Sophie / Medicore IT: Confirm whether CMK in your KMS is required or Redwood-managed keys are acceptable. (Due: 2025-07-25)
2) Ben (Redwood SE): Map which Dedicated SKUs meet your latency and throughput targets and list the residual controls (Due: 2025-07-24).
3) Karthik (Redwood Infra): Prepare a short spreadsheet showing the audit log export surfaces we can provide from Dedicated vs Private deployments (Due: 2025-07-24).
4) Aisha (me): Consolidate answers and propose a recommended deployment mode with tradeoffs (Due: 2025-07-27).

I attached the checklist and a short Medicore-focused security brief for reference. If you prefer, we can run a brief 30-min technical deep-dive next week with your infra leads.

Cheers,

Aisha Rahman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Email: aisha.rahman@redwood.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0143

From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@medicore.com>

Cc: Medicore IT <it@medicore.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jul 2025 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up & acceptance checklist: Dedicated vs Private VPC

Thanks Aisha — useful summary. Quick answers from the security council:
- We prefer customer-controlled CMKs in our KMS for anything touching PHI-derived features. Redwood-managed keys are acceptable for non-PHI telemetry.
- Network: we need VPC peering with private endpoints; IP allowlist is not sufficient for the production model.
- Audit logs: we need immutable export to our SIEM (Splunk) and retention for 7 years for a subset of logs.
- Persistence: snapshots must be deletable only by Medicore or with documented approval process.

Can you confirm whether Dedicated can support VPC peering and customer CMKs, or if that combination requires Private VPC/on-prem? We are leaning Private VPC but want to understand the cost/performance tradeoffs before locking anything down.

Also looping in two Medicore infra folks to schedule the technical deep-dive if needed: Samir Patel (samir.patel@medicore.com) and Lia Gomez (lia.gomez@medicore.com).

—Sophie
Director of Data Products, Medicore

Subject: RE: Follow-up & acceptance checklist: Dedicated vs Private VPC

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clarity. Short answers from the SE side and a proposed path: 

1) Dedicated + VPC peering: We do support VPC peering / PrivateLink for a number of Dedicated customers today. That gets you private network connectivity while we still manage the infra. However, Dedicated with customer CMKs is only supported in a limited configuration today (requires HSM/KMS integration work and an additional security review).

2) Audit log export: For Dedicated we can stream audit/log exports to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) — the retention window is governed by your SIEM, we can provide immutable log signing and export hooks. For Private VPC/on-prem, you maintain full copy of audit logs by default.

3) Snapshot deletion control: We can build a custodial workflow where snapshots are flagged and require Medicore approval before deletion in Dedicated; for Private VPC you own snapshots fully.

Suggested pragmatic path to de-risk:
- Phase 1 (Proof-of-Concept): Provision Dedicated with VPC peering + CMK pilot (limited dataset, dev region). This minimizes time-to-demo while we validate key integration and audit exports.
- Phase 2 (If controls unacceptable): Move to Private VPC/on-prem for production cutover.

I'll attach a short matrix with which controls map to which deployment (attached as redwood-deployment-acceptance-checklist.pdf). Can we plan the technical deep-dive tomorrow 30 min? I can cover the Dedicated controls and Karthik can explain the KMS integration effort.

Best,
Ben Carter
